Portland experiential technology pros, how the heck did none of you tell me about CETI?!? 🤬

If you don't know CETI, they are a non-profit organization that focuses on emerging technologies, creative workshops, and interactive public art exhibits.

I got to take a tour of their new space, and MY GOODNESS Y'ALL!!! It's basically an experience agency that you can use for free.

Let me say that again: this is all of the hardware of an experience agency that, somehow, you can use...

...for free.

Want VR helmets? They've got that.
3D printers? Covered.
Soldering tools? Of course.
NUCs? Yup.
Projectors? Yuuuuuup.
Tablets? Duh.
LED Walls? More like Y-E-S walls.

Think about how lucky we are to have these folks in our city. I mean, I'm looking around the room and I see recreational creative techs, pros, networkers, connecters - folks of all types, connected by a neon strobing chain:

The passion we all have for creative technology. 🔥

So I'm hooked. I can't wait to see what I can do to help this community out. The opportunities CETI gives folks can only be replicated by college or work experience, typically, and I'll say this louder for the folks in the back:

IT'S FREE!!!

There will be another meeting in August to talk about the art show they'll be having later on in the year. I think there are real opportunities for local pros and their companies to get involved and make a huge impact on the local community. I believe this could have a ripple effect that would help PDX get its experiential tech swagger back.

I'm resisting the urge to tag a bunch of industry peeps who I think would make great additions to CETI... resisssstingggg...

Hey design network, have you thought about using generative AI for building plugins and scripts for Adobe CC apps?

Having had to build scripts for Adobe products in the past, let me just say that the experience leaves a lot to be desired. The docs aren't great, the community is small, and often the interpreter is wildly out of date.

Using an AI agent like ChatGPT develop time saving scripts is the way to go. 💯

👇 Check this video out for inspiration.

Most experiential agencies are sitting on a platform problem, and nobody wants to admit it.

Why?

Because everyone's budget goes to the next build, and the CMS holding it all together is duct tape from three projects ago. I've spent years now building and rebuilding these systems, and it's always the same story — the platform gets touched last and trusted LEAST.

That's backwards. The platform is the thing that makes every future project cheaper, not the thing you starve to ship the next one.

Maybe I should just start billing agencies for the CMS work they keep avoiding. Half joking. Mostly not. 🧐

Sure, it's extremely useful for refactoring, documenting, and writing tests for single files, but why not scan my entire project when you've got access to it?!?

Well, it turns out that the GitHub team felt the same way and you can actually do this with Copilot... TODAY! 🔥🔥🔥

OpenAI's ChatGPT turns 1 today! 🎉 This got me thinking about how much it has impacted my life so far:

✅ It has made me a much better developer. Being able to pair program with an LLM that has extensive knowledge of best practices and has a solid understanding of programming is immensely valuable.

✅ It has made me a significantly more marketable job candidate. I was able to produce the best resume I've ever had by bouncing ideas off of it and comparing my skills with what jobs are looking for.

✅ Finally, it has given me a new creative outlet. I love using it to generate images with DALL-E 3, write stories about ridiculous nonsense, and anything else I can think of to keep me occupied.

If there's one thing that I've learned, it's that it's ultimately still a tool and NOT a replacement. In other words, I don't assume that the code it writes is great, nor do I just take the resume advice that it gives me as gospel. In fact, a lot of times it's kinda crappy. However, I've learned how to use it as an intelligent, supremely well educated, and non-judgemental partner in a lot of the tasks that I do every single day.

Here's to the future. 🥂
